instruction: Lis la question, puis écoute l’histoire en anglais. Pour l’entendre encore, appuie sur Écouter. Le lexique est affiché.

items.prompt:
On Sunday, Emma goes to the market with her dad.
First, they buy apples.
Then, they buy bread.
At the end, they eat an ice cream.
items.question: Qu’achètent Emma et son père en premier ?
items.spoken: On Sunday, Emma goes to the market with her dad. First, they buy apples. Then, they buy bread. At the end, they eat an ice cream.
items.hint: En premier se dit first. Écoute ce qui vient juste après.
items.explanation: First, they buy apples = d’abord, ils achètent des pommes. Le pain (bread) vient ensuite, avec then, et la glace à la fin.

items.prompt:
Max wakes up at seven.
First, he has a shower.
Then, he has breakfast.
At the end, he takes the bus to school.
items.question: Que fait Max juste après sa douche ?
items.spoken: Max wakes up at seven. First, he has a shower. Then, he has breakfast. At the end, he takes the bus to school.
items.hint: La douche, c’est a shower. Écoute la phrase qui suit, avec then.
items.explanation: First, a shower (la douche) ; then, breakfast (le petit déjeuner). Le bus vient à la fin, et il se réveille (wakes up) avant la douche.

First, her friends arrive at four.
Then, they play games in the garden.
At the end, Nora opens her presents.
items.question: Que fait Nora à la fin de la fête ?
items.spoken: It’s Nora’s birthday. First, her friends arrive at four. Then, they play games in the garden. At the end, Nora opens her presents.
items.hint: À la fin se dit at the end. Écoute la dernière phrase.
items.explanation: At the end, Nora opens her presents = à la fin, Nora ouvre ses cadeaux (a present = un cadeau). Les jeux dans le jardin viennent avant, avec then.

items.prompt:
Josh goes to the cinema with his sister, Kate.
First, Kate buys the tickets.
Then, Josh buys some popcorn.
At the end, they walk home.
items.question: Qui achète le pop-corn ?
items.spoken: Josh goes to the cinema with his sister, Kate. First, Kate buys the tickets. Then, Josh buys some popcorn. At the end, they walk home.
items.hint: Écoute la phrase où l’on entend popcorn : quel prénom juste avant buys ?
items.explanation: Then, Josh buys some popcorn = ensuite, Josh achète du pop-corn. Kate, sa sœur, achète les billets (the tickets) en premier.

items.prompt:
Lena has got a busy week.
On Monday, she goes to the library.
On Tuesday, she plays basketball.
On Thursday, she has a piano lesson.
items.question: Quel jour Lena joue-t-elle au basket ?
items.spoken: Lena has got a busy week. On Monday, she goes to the library. On Tuesday, she plays basketball. On Thursday, she has a piano lesson.
items.hint: Tuesday ou Thursday ? Écoute le début du mot.
items.explanation: On Tuesday, she plays basketball = le mardi, elle joue au basket. Tuesday commence par « tiou » ; Thursday (jeudi), avec th, c’est le piano.

items.prompt:
Ryan is late for school.
First, he can’t find his shoes.
Then, he misses the bus.
At the end, he runs to school.
items.question: À la fin, comment Ryan va-t-il à l’école ?
items.spoken: Ryan is late for school. First, he can’t find his shoes. Then, he misses the bus. At the end, he runs to school.
items.hint: Il rate le bus (he misses the bus). Écoute la dernière phrase : quel verbe entends-tu après he ?
items.explanation: At the end, he runs to school = à la fin, il court jusqu’à l’école. Il a raté le bus (he misses the bus) : il ne le prend pas.

At the end, they put the cake in the oven.

choices: Elles mettent le gâteau au four

items.prompt:
Adam and his mum go to the beach.
First, Adam swims in the sea.
Then, he plays football on the sand.
At the end, they have dinner in a small restaurant.
items.question: Où Adam et sa mère dînent-ils ?
items.spoken: Adam and his mum go to the beach. First, Adam swims in the sea. Then, he plays football on the sand. At the end, they have dinner in a small restaurant.
items.hint: Dîner se dit have dinner. Écoute la dernière phrase.
items.explanation: They have dinner in a small restaurant = ils dînent dans un petit restaurant. La plage (the beach), c’est pour nager et jouer au foot sur le sable.
